pinyin: rú zhuì wǔ lǐ wù zhōng
literal: as if · fall into · five · li · fog · inside
natural: as if lost in a five-mile fog

meaning.en: To be completely baffled and unable to make sense of what is going on.
meaning.zh: 好像掉进了五里长的大雾里，形容事情不明白、摸不着头脑。

examples.zh: 听了半天，我还是如坠五里雾中。
examples.en: After listening for ages, I was still completely in the dark.

examples.zh: 这套新系统的操作说明让大家如坠五里雾中。
examples.en: The instructions for the new system left everyone baffled.

examples.zh: 他们说的专业术语太多，我如坠五里雾中。
examples.en: They used so much jargon that I was totally lost.

usage.en: Predicate; also written 如坠五里雾. 五里雾 refers to a legendary fog five li wide made by the Han scholar Zhang Kai.
usage.zh: 多作谓语，也说“如坠五里雾”。“五里雾”相传是东汉张楷所作的五里大雾。

pinyin: méi huā xiāng zì kǔ hán lái
literal: plum · blossom · fragrant · from · bitter · cold · come
natural: plum blossom's fragrance comes from bitter cold

meaning.en: Success and excellence are earned through hardship.
meaning.zh: 梅花的香气来自严寒的磨炼，比喻成就来自艰苦的努力。

equivalents: sweet are the fruits of adversity

examples.zh: 梅花香自苦寒来，他的成功是十年苦练换来的。
examples.en: Plum fragrance comes from bitter cold; his success was bought with ten years of hard training.

examples.zh: 老师用梅花香自苦寒来勉励大家。
examples.en: The teacher encouraged us with the saying that plum fragrance comes from bitter cold.

examples.zh: 梅花香自苦寒来，没有一夜成名的奇迹。
examples.en: Plum fragrance comes from bitter cold; there is no miracle of overnight fame.

usage.en: Often paired with 宝剑锋从磨砺出. Popular in speeches, school mottos and essays.
usage.zh: 常与“宝剑锋从磨砺出”对举，多用于演讲、勉励和作文。

synonyms: 吃得苦中苦，方为人上人

natural: to shoot a rider, first shoot his horse

meaning.en: To defeat an enemy, first strike at what he depends on; go for the key point first.
meaning.zh: 要射中骑兵，先射他的马，比喻对付敌人要先抓住关键。

equivalents: cut off the head of the snake

examples.zh: 射人先射马，要整垮对手，先断他的货源。
examples.en: To bring down a rival, first cut his supply: strike at what he depends on.

examples.zh: 射人先射马，足球队常先盯防对方的核心球员。
examples.en: Shoot the horse before the rider: teams often mark the opponent's key player first.

examples.zh: 射人先射马，擒贼先擒王，说的都是抓关键。
examples.en: 'Shoot the horse first' and 'catch the chief first' both mean going for the key point.

story.en: Du Fu's Qian Chusai poem reads, 'To shoot a man, shoot his horse first; to catch bandits, catch their chief first' (射人先射马，擒贼先擒王).
story.zh: 杜甫《前出塞九首》：“挽弓当挽强，用箭当用长。射人先射马，擒贼先擒王。”

usage.en: The couplet continues 擒贼先擒王. Used in strategy and business talk.
usage.zh: 原诗下句为“擒贼先擒王”，常用于谋略、商业场合。

natural: at the peak, decline must follow

meaning.en: Whatever reaches its peak of prosperity must then decline.
meaning.zh: 事物发展到极盛，就一定会走向衰落。

equivalents: what goes up must come down

examples.zh: 盛极必衰，再强大的王朝也有终结的一天。
examples.en: What peaks must decline; even the mightiest dynasty has its end.

examples.zh: 这家公司扩张太快，盛极必衰，不久便陷入危机。
examples.en: The company expanded too fast; having peaked, it declined and soon fell into crisis.

examples.zh: 盛极必衰，他在事业巅峰时选择了退隐。
examples.en: Knowing what rises must fall, he retired at the height of his career.

usage.en: Predicate or clause; a reflective, general principle. Also 物极必反 (extremes reverse).
usage.zh: 多作谓语或分句，表达一种通则。近义有“物极必反”。

natural: cheap things are never good

meaning.en: Cheap goods are usually poor in quality.
meaning.zh: 价钱便宜的东西质量往往不好。

equivalents: you get what you pay for
cheap goods are dear in the end

examples.zh: 便宜没好货，这双鞋穿两天就开胶了。
examples.en: You get what you pay for; these shoes fell apart in two days.

examples.zh: 买家电别光看价格，便宜没好货。
examples.en: Don't judge appliances by price alone; cheap goods are rarely good.

examples.zh: 她总说便宜没好货，宁愿多花钱买品牌。
examples.en: She always says cheap means poor and pays more for a good brand.

usage.en: Usually paired with 好货不便宜. Used by shoppers, sometimes as a counter to bargain-hunting.
usage.zh: 常与“好货不便宜”并说，多用于购物场合，常用来回应贪便宜的做法。

natural: suspicion breeds hidden ghosts

meaning.en: Once you become suspicious, you imagine threats that are not there.
meaning.zh: 心里起了疑虑，就会胡思乱想，觉得处处有可怕的东西。

examples.zh: 他总觉得同事在背后议论他，真是疑心生暗鬼。
examples.en: He kept feeling colleagues were gossiping behind his back; suspicion breeds ghosts.

examples.zh: 夜里听到响声，疑心生暗鬼，她一夜没睡。
examples.en: Hearing a noise at night, she imagined the worst and did not sleep.

examples.zh: 别疑心生暗鬼，对方只是路过。
examples.en: Don't let suspicion conjure up ghosts; he was only passing by.

usage.en: Predicate or clause; used to caution against baseless suspicion.
usage.zh: 多作谓语或分句，用于劝人不要无端猜疑。

natural: the day does not supply enough time

meaning.en: To be so busy that one has no spare time at all.
meaning.zh: 事情太多，一天的时间都不够用，形容极其忙碌。

equivalents: not have a moment to spare

examples.zh: 年底总结、考核、会议，让他日不暇给。
examples.en: Year-end reviews, assessments and meetings left him without a spare moment.

examples.zh: 新店开业这几天，老板日不暇给。
examples.en: In the days around the shop's opening, the owner had no time to breathe.

examples.zh: 总统访问期间，外交部门日不暇给。
examples.en: During the president's visit, the diplomats were rushed off their feet.

usage.en: Predicate; formal. Do not confuse with 目不暇给 / 目不暇接 (too much to see).
usage.zh: 多作谓语，书面语。注意不要与“目不暇给／目不暇接”（东西太多看不过来）混淆。

literal: fortune · ah · misfortune · where · lies hidden
natural: fortune is where misfortune lies in wait

meaning.en: Misfortune lurks within good fortune; success carries the seeds of trouble.
meaning.zh: 福运之中隐藏着祸患，好事可能转为坏事。

examples.zh: 福兮祸所伏，他得意忘形，结果栽了跟头。
examples.en: Misfortune lurks in good fortune; he grew complacent and came a cropper.

examples.zh: 福兮祸所伏，中了大奖的人未必快乐。
examples.en: Good fortune may hide trouble; lottery winners are not always happy.

examples.zh: 福兮祸所伏，越顺利越要小心。
examples.en: Trouble hides in luck, so the smoother things go, the more careful one should be.

story.en: Laozi: 'Misfortune is what good fortune leans on; good fortune is where misfortune lies hidden' (祸兮福之所倚，福兮祸之所伏).
story.zh: 《老子》第五十八章：“祸兮福之所倚，福兮祸之所伏。”

date.zh: 春秋末至战国 · 前6—前4世纪
date.en: late Spring and Autumn to Warring States, 6th–4th c. BC

usage.en: The full pair is 祸兮福所倚，福兮祸所伏; the Laozi text has 之 in the second half: 福兮祸之所伏. Used to caution against complacency.
usage.zh: 全联为“祸兮福所倚，福兮祸所伏”；《老子》原文作“福兮祸之所伏”。多用于提醒人不要得意忘形。

natural: flee defeated to Maicheng

meaning.en: To suffer a crushing defeat after a period of success; to be defeated and left with no way out.
meaning.zh: 指关羽兵败退守麦城，比喻在事业上遭到惨败。

examples.zh: 这支球队连胜之后，在决赛中败走麦城。
examples.en: After a winning streak, the team met its Waterloo in the final.

examples.zh: 他在股市里一路高歌，最后却败走麦城。
examples.en: He did brilliantly in the stock market, only to come to grief at the end.

examples.zh: 新品牌进入中国市场不到两年便败走麦城。
examples.en: The new brand was beaten within two years of entering the Chinese market.

story.en: Chapter 76 of Romance of the Three Kingdoms is titled 'Xu Gongming Fights at the Mian River; Guan Yunchang Is Defeated and Flees to Maicheng' (关云长败走麦城).
story.zh: 《三国演义》第七十六回回目：“徐公明大战沔水　关云长败走麦城”。

date.en: late Yuan to early Ming, 14th c.

usage.en: Predicate; from the fall of Guan Yu in 219, who retreated to Maicheng and was captured and executed by Wu. Often used of a proud hero's defeat.
usage.zh: 多作谓语，典故出自关羽在公元219年兵败退守麦城，后被东吴擒杀。常指骄傲自大者遭到惨败。

pinyin: bīng jiā bì zhēng zhī dì
natural: a place every strategist must fight for

meaning.en: A location of such strategic importance that every army wants to seize it.
meaning.zh: 军事家一定要争夺的战略要地，也比喻各方都想夺取的关键位置。

examples.zh: 襄阳是三国时期的兵家必争之地。
examples.en: Xiangyang was a place every army fought for in the Three Kingdoms period.

examples.zh: 这个交通枢纽成了各大电商兵家必争之地。
examples.en: This transport hub has become a prize all the big e-commerce firms fight for.

examples.zh: 新能源汽车市场如今是兵家必争之地。
examples.en: The new-energy vehicle market is now a battleground every firm wants.

usage.en: Attributive or object; often used figuratively of business markets.
usage.zh: 多作定语、宾语，现多比喻商业上必须抢占的市场。

natural: bright eyes that glance well

meaning.en: Bright, lively eyes; used of a beautiful woman's expressive gaze.
meaning.zh: 眼睛明亮灵活，善于顾盼，形容女子眼睛美丽有神。

examples.zh: 她明眸善睐，一笑起来更动人。
examples.en: With her bright, expressive eyes, she is even more charming when she smiles.

examples.zh: 小说里的女主角明眸善睐，让人难忘。
examples.en: The heroine of the novel, with her sparkling eyes, is unforgettable.

examples.zh: 这位演员明眸善睐，镜头前很有表现力。
examples.en: The actress has bright eyes and is very expressive on camera.

story.en: Cao Zhi describes the goddess of the Luo River: 'Bright eyes that glance well, dimples beneath her cheekbones' (明眸善睐，靥辅承权).
story.zh: 曹植《洛神赋》：“明眸善睐，靥辅承权。”

usage.en: Predicate or attributive; literary praise of a woman's looks, usually with 皓齿.
usage.zh: 多作谓语、定语，多用来赞美女子容貌，常与“皓齿”连用。

natural: dazzle everyone seated around

meaning.en: To amaze everyone present with one's dazzling beauty or splendid appearance.
meaning.zh: 以出众的美貌或亮眼的装扮让在座的人为之惊叹。

examples.zh: 她一袭红裙出场，艳惊四座。
examples.en: She entered in a red dress and turned every head.

examples.zh: 颁奖礼上，女星们争奇斗艳，她却艳惊四座。
examples.en: At the awards the actresses all competed to dazzle, but she took everyone's breath away.

examples.zh: 新娘的婚纱设计独特，艳惊四座。
examples.en: The bride's gown was so distinctive that it astonished all the guests.

usage.en: Predicate; usually of a woman's looks or outfit at a social event. Compare 语惊四座 and 技惊四座.
usage.zh: 多作谓语，多用于女子在社交场合的容貌或装扮。可比较“语惊四座”“技惊四座”。

natural: record events by tying cords

meaning.en: The ancient practice of recording events by tying knots in cords, before writing existed.
meaning.zh: 上古没有文字时，用在绳子上打结的办法来记事。

examples.zh: 博物馆里展出了古人结绳记事的复原品。
examples.en: The museum displays a reconstruction of how the ancients kept records with knotted cords.

examples.zh: 在文字发明之前，人们靠结绳记事。
examples.en: Before writing was invented, people kept records by tying knots.

examples.zh: 他从小就听老人讲结绳记事的故事。
examples.en: From childhood he heard elders tell of recording events with knotted cords.

story.en: The Appended Judgements say that in high antiquity 'people governed by tying cords' (上古结绳而治), and later sages replaced this with written records (后世圣人易之以书契).
story.zh: 《周易·系辞下》：“上古结绳而治，后世圣人易之以书契。”

date.zh: 西周至战国 · 前9—前3世纪
date.en: Western Zhou to Warring States, 9th–3rd c. BC

usage.en: A descriptive phrase for primitive practice; used literally in history and figuratively of very simple methods.
usage.zh: 描述上古时代的记事方式，多用于历史介绍，也比喻方法极其原始。

natural: laws and decrees grow ever more numerous

meaning.en: The more laws and rules are issued, the more crime and trouble arise.
meaning.zh: 法律禁令越多越严，盗贼和纠纷反而越多。

equivalents: too many rules breed more violations
the more laws, the more criminals

examples.zh: 法令滋彰，盗贼多有，老子这句话至今发人深省。
examples.en: 'The more laws, the more thieves', as Laozi said, still gives food for thought.

examples.zh: 有人批评繁琐的规定是法令滋彰，反而增加了负担。
examples.en: Some criticise the pile of rules as counterproductive: more regulations, more burdens.

examples.zh: 法令滋彰未必带来更好的秩序。
examples.en: More laws do not necessarily bring better order.

story.en: Laozi: 'The more laws and decrees are displayed, the more thieves and bandits there are' (法令滋彰，盗贼多有).
story.zh: 《老子》第五十七章：“法令滋彰，盗贼多有。”

date.zh: 春秋末至战国 · 前6—前4世纪
date.en: late Spring and Autumn to Warring States, 6th–4th c. BC

usage.en: Predicate or quoted clause; from a Daoist view that over-regulation backfires. Often quoted with 盗贼多有.
usage.zh: 多作谓语或引用分句，体现道家反对繁苛政令的看法，常与“盗贼多有”连用。

natural: an oyster's ailment becomes a pearl

meaning.en: A pearl forms from an oyster's irritation; fine results can come out of suffering.
meaning.zh: 蚌因沙粒侵入受伤而生成珍珠，比喻艰难痛苦之中产生出优秀的成果。

examples.zh: 他在病中完成了这部小说，真可谓蚌病成珠。
examples.en: He finished this novel while ill, truly a pearl born of the oyster's pain.

examples.zh: 许多艺术杰作是蚌病成珠，出于苦难。
examples.en: Many masterpieces are pearls from the oyster's pain, born of suffering.

examples.zh: 蚌病成珠，困境反而逼出了她的才华。
examples.en: Like an oyster making a pearl, hardship drew out her talent.

usage.en: Predicate or comment on achievement; literary. Related to 老蚌生珠 (a gifted child born late to elderly parents) but not the same meaning.
usage.zh: 多作谓语或对成就的评语，书面语。与“老蚌生珠”（老来得贤子）相关，但含义不同。

natural: write a poem on a red leaf

meaning.en: A romantic tale of lovers brought together by a poem written on a red leaf; also a fond figure for an unexpected romantic connection.
meaning.zh: 唐代传说中宫女在红叶上题诗，随水流出，终与题者结为夫妇，后用来指因诗传情、天赐良缘。

equivalents: a love note sent on the wind

examples.zh: 小说里写红叶题诗的故事，浪漫动人。
examples.en: The story of the poem on a red leaf is touchingly romantic.

examples.zh: 两人以诗相识，传为红叶题诗的佳话。
examples.en: The couple met through poetry, a story told like the legend of the poem on the red leaf.

examples.zh: 秋天的御沟边，游客想起红叶题诗的典故。
examples.en: By the autumn palace stream, visitors recall the legend of the poem on a red leaf.

usage.en: Mostly allusive or literary. The legend is told in several Tang and later sources with different named couples.
usage.zh: 多作典故或文学用语。唐代及后世多种记载，人物说法不一。

natural: skin like congealed fat

meaning.en: Skin that is smooth, white and delicate, like solidified suet.
meaning.zh: 皮肤像凝固的油脂一样白嫩光滑。

examples.zh: 古人形容美女，常说肤如凝脂。
examples.en: The ancients often described beauties as having skin like congealed fat.

examples.zh: 画中女子肤如凝脂，眉目如画。
examples.en: The woman in the painting has flawless skin and a face like a picture.

examples.zh: 广告词说用了这款面霜，也能肤如凝脂。
examples.en: The advert claims this cream gives you flawless skin.

story.en: The ode describing Zhuang Jiang's beauty says: 'Hands like soft shoots, skin like congealed fat' (手如柔荑，肤如凝脂).
story.zh: 《诗经·卫风·硕人》：“手如柔荑，肤如凝脂。”

date.zh: 西周初至春秋中叶 · 前11—前6世纪
date.en: early Western Zhou to mid Spring and Autumn, 11th–6th c. BC

usage.en: Predicate; literary praise of a woman's skin. 'Suet' is the ancient simile, which sounds odd to modern ears.
usage.zh: 多作谓语，书面语，用于赞美女子肌肤。以油脂作比是古人的比喻。

natural: each excels in a field of their own

meaning.en: Each of several people excels in a different area, or each has strengths of their own.
meaning.zh: 各人在不同方面各有所长，各自有擅长的领域。

equivalents: each in a class of their own

examples.zh: 两位画家各擅胜场，一工山水，一工人物。
examples.en: The two painters each have their own strengths, one in landscapes, the other in figures.

examples.zh: 两支球队各擅胜场，比赛十分精彩。
examples.en: The two teams each have their strong points, so the match was thrilling.

examples.zh: 这几位歌手各擅胜场，难分高下。
examples.en: These singers each excel in their own way and it is hard to rank them.

usage.en: Predicate; formal and written, usually of two or more equals.
usage.zh: 多作谓语，书面语，通常指两方或多方各有千秋。

pinyin: yī zhī yī yè zǒng guān qíng
literal: one · twig · one · leaf · always · concerns · feeling
natural: every twig and leaf stirs my feelings

meaning.en: A conscientious official cares about every detail of the people's welfare, down to the last twig and leaf.
meaning.zh: 一枝一叶都牵动着我的情怀，比喻官员对百姓的疾苦时刻关心。

equivalents: have the people's welfare at heart

examples.zh: 一枝一叶总关情，他把群众的小事当成大事。
examples.en: Every twig and leaf concerns him; he treats the people's small problems as big ones.

examples.zh: 市长在讲话中引用“一枝一叶总关情”，表达了为民之心。
examples.en: The mayor quoted 'every twig and leaf stirs my feelings' in his speech to show he cares for the people.

examples.zh: 好医生对病人一枝一叶总关情。
examples.en: A good doctor cares about every little thing about his patients.

origin.source: 郑板桥《潍县署中画竹呈年伯包大中丞括》

story.en: Zheng Banqiao, a county magistrate, wrote: 'Lying in my office, I hear the bamboo rustle and suspect it is the people's suffering; small official that I am, every twig and leaf concerns me' (衙斋卧听萧萧竹，疑是民间疾苦声。些小吾曹州县吏，一枝一叶总关情).
story.zh: 郑板桥：“衙斋卧听萧萧竹，疑是民间疾苦声。些小吾曹州县吏，一枝一叶总关情。”

usage.en: Quoted when praising officials or leaders who care about ordinary people; the poem continues 衙斋卧听萧萧竹，疑是民间疾苦声.
usage.zh: 多在称赞官员关心民间疾苦时引用，与“衙斋卧听萧萧竹，疑是民间疾苦声”连读。

synonyms: 衙斋卧听萧萧竹，疑是民间疾苦声
variants: 些小吾曹州县吏，一枝一叶总关情

pinyin: wēi jí cún wáng zhī qiū
natural: a time of danger and urgency, of survival or ruin

meaning.en: A critical moment on which survival or destruction depends.
meaning.zh: 形容形势危险紧迫，到了决定生死存亡的关键时刻。

examples.zh: 国家正处于危急存亡之秋，每个人都应尽一份力。
examples.en: The country is at a make-or-break moment, and everyone should do their part.

examples.zh: 公司面临破产，正是危急存亡之秋。
examples.en: The company faces bankruptcy; it is a critical hour.

examples.zh: 抗战时期是中华民族危急存亡之秋。
examples.en: The War of Resistance was a time of mortal peril for the Chinese nation.

story.en: Zhuge Liang wrote to the young emperor: 'This is truly a time of danger and urgency, when survival or ruin hangs in the balance' (此诚危急存亡之秋也).
story.zh: 诸葛亮《出师表》：“今天下三分，益州疲弊，此诚危急存亡之秋也。”

usage.en: Usually with 此诚…也 or 值此. 秋 here means 'time, crucial moment', not autumn.
usage.zh: 常说“此诚危急存亡之秋也”或“值此危急存亡之秋”。这里的“秋”指时刻、关键时期，不是秋天。

synonyms: 中华民族到了最危险的时候

natural: the Dao follows what is natural

meaning.en: The Dao takes its pattern from the spontaneous way of nature; one should follow the natural course of things.
meaning.zh: 道以自然为法则，指顺应事物本来的规律，不加人为干预。

examples.zh: 道法自然，园林设计应顺应地形。
examples.en: The Dao follows nature, so garden design should follow the lie of the land.

examples.zh: 他信奉道法自然，不强求事业成败。
examples.en: He believes in following nature's way and does not force success.

examples.zh: 养生之道，贵在道法自然。
examples.en: The key to healthy living is following the natural order.

story.en: Laozi: 'Man follows the earth, earth follows heaven, heaven follows the Dao, and the Dao follows what is natural' (人法地，地法天，天法道，道法自然).
story.zh: 《老子》第二十五章：“人法地，地法天，天法道，道法自然。”

date.zh: 春秋末至战国 · 前6—前4世纪
date.en: late Spring and Autumn to Warring States, 6th–4th c. BC

usage.en: The full Laozi line: 人法地，地法天，天法道，道法自然. Often quoted in discussions of ecology, wellbeing and design.
usage.zh: 老子原句为“人法地，地法天，天法道，道法自然”。常见于生态、养生和设计等话题。
